audience.programmeDescription: The joint University of Twente and VU Amsterdam Creative Technology degree combines computing, electronics, human-centred design and interactive media. The Amsterdam example includes Humane by Design, with work on future scenarios and fairness in data science.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR options explore creative computing and product design, AI and smart systems, or human interaction with technology. The Amsterdam curriculum combines its fairness and design work with physical computing, interactive installations and an individual graduation project.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC example includes 30 EC of approved elective study and a 30 EC graduation semester.

componentNotes.m5-humane-design: Includes Fairness in Data Science and a project on designing futures. Module eight includes Dangerous Design.
componentNotes.y3-electives: Entry normally requires all 60 EC from year one and at least 30 EC from year two.
componentNotes.y3-project: Normally follows completion of modules 1–8. The 5 EC first part must be completed before the 15 EC second part.

notes.text: UCR offers related study in computing, product prototyping, cognition and communication. Twente integrates electronics, physical computing and interactive installations through a sequence of studio and laboratory projects.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
